title: Finite-cover tube decomposition and identification of the ordinary comparison
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $g:U\to S$ arbitrary, and $X_U=X\times_SU$. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring killed by an integer invertible on $S$ and $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$, in the constant-module category of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Choose $z_U=(x_U,b_U,c_U)$ in $V_{f_U}$ with image $z=(x,b,c)$ in $V_f$. Strict localizations and the chosen specializations define the tubes
$$M=X_{(x)}\times_{S_{(f(x))}}S_{(b)},\qquad N=(X_U)_{(x_U)}\times_{U_{(f_U(x_U))}}U_{(b_U)}.$$
There is a natural map $N\to M$. Under the oriented-point cohomology isomorphisms [lem-trf-oriented-point-cohomology], the stalk at $z_U$ of the ordinary comparison $\beta_g:v_g^*R\Psi_fK\to R\Psi_{f_U}K_U$ is the restriction map $R\Gamma(M,K)\to R\Gamma(N,K_U)$.

Put $S_0=S_{(f(x))}$, $U_0=U_{(f_U(x_U))}$ and let $P\to S_0$ be finite surjective. Set $P_q=P^{\times_{S_0}(q+1)}$, $Q_q=U_0\times_{S_0}P_q$, $A_q=R\Gamma(M\times_{S_0}P_q,K)$ and $B_q=R\Gamma(N\times_{U_0}Q_q,K_U)$. Both families have the restriction maps of their augmented Cech diagrams. The first cover is a finite disjoint union of Milnor tubes for $f_{P_q}$ indexed by $I_q=\pi_0((P_q)_b)$; the second is the corresponding finite disjoint union for $f_{Q_q}$ indexed by $J_q=\pi_0((Q_q)_{b_U})$. Here $b$ and $b_U$ also denote their canonical lifts to $S_0$ and $U_0$. The resulting derived section decompositions are finite products. Whenever projection identifies $J_q$ bijectively with $I_q$, the map $A_q\to B_q$ is the product of the stalks of the ordinary comparisons for the Cartesian squares with base map $Q_q\to P_q$, coefficient the pullback of $K$, and the corresponding lifted specializations. These are identifications of the actual restriction maps, compatible with their cofaces; no base-change invertibility or truncated descent is assumed.
